title: CIS 223 · Sorting & Selection
markdown:
<!-- nodal-panel:sec-overview:visible:title=Overview -->

**Sorting Algorithms**
- **Comparison Sort**: Insertion, Merge, Heap, Quick
- **Non-comparison Sort**: Counting, Radix, Bucket
- **Selection**: Quickselect

**Core Distinctions**
- **Comparison Sort**: relative order comes strictly from comparing elements.
- **Non-comparison Sort**: uses structure of keys, digits, or value ranges.
- **Selection**: finds a specific rank without fully sorting.

**Lower Bound**
- Any comparison-based sorting algorithm has a lower bound of $\Omega(n \log n)$.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-comparison-sort:visible:title=Comparison%20Sort -->

Obtains relative order strictly via pairwise element comparisons.

- Covered algorithms: Insertion Sort, Merge Sort, Heap Sort, Quick Sort.
- Theoretical limit: $\Omega(n \log n)$ comparisons in the worst case.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-insertion-sort:visible:parent=sec-comparison-sort:title=Insertion%20Sort -->

Grow a sorted prefix, one key at a time.

![Insertion Sort: Grow a sorted prefix, one key at a time](study/assets/asset-insertion-sort-%E6%8F%92%E5%85%A5%E6%8E%92%E5%BA%8F%EF%BC%9A%E9%80%90%E6%AD%A5%E6%9E%84%E5%BB%BA%E6%9C%89%E5%BA%8F%E5%89%8D%E7%BC%80.png)

- **Sorted prefix invariant**: at step $i$, prefix $A[0 \dots i-1]$ is already sorted.
- **Inner operation sequence**: find position $\to$ shift elements right $\to$ insert key into vacant slot.
- **Order direction**:
  - Ascending: shift elements where $A[j] > \text{key}$.
  - Descending: shift elements where $A[j] < \text{key}$.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-insertion-code:visible:parent=sec-insertion-sort:title=Code -->

```java
for (int i = 1; i < a.length; i++) {
    Key key = a[i];          // current key to insert
    int j = i - 1;
    // find position & shift
    while (j >= 0 && a[j].compareTo(key) > 0) {
        a[j + 1] = a[j];     // shift right
        j--;
    }
    a[j + 1] = key;          // insert into vacant position
}
```

- `i = 1` starts from the second element (a single element prefix $A[0]$ is trivially sorted).
- Loop test `j >= 0` must precede `compareTo` to guard against index out-of-bounds.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-merge-sort:visible:parent=sec-comparison-sort:title=Merge%20Sort -->

Divide into halves, recursively sort, then merge the sorted halves.

![Merge Sort: Divide into halves, recursively sort, then merge](study/assets/asset-merge-sort-%E5%BD%92%E5%B9%B6%E6%8E%92%E5%BA%8F%E7%AE%97%E6%B3%95%E5%9B%BE%E8%A7%A3.png)

- **Base case**: stop when subarray size $\le 1$.
- **Split point**: `mid` is an index / split position ($lo + (hi - lo) / 2$), never the element value stored at $S[n/2]$.
- **Merge contract**: takes two already-sorted subarrays and produces one combined sorted array.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-merge-code-bugs:visible:parent=sec-merge-sort:title=Code%20%26%20Bug%20Recognition -->

```java
private static void sort(Key[] a, Key[] aux, int lo, int hi) {
    if (hi <= lo) return; // base case: size <= 1
    int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
    sort(a, aux, lo, mid);
    sort(a, aux, mid + 1, hi);
    merge(a, aux, lo, mid, hi);
}
```

**Common Quiz Traps & Bugs**
- **Base case omission**: `if (hi <= lo) return;` must stop for 1 element. Stopping only on 0 elements leads to infinite recursion.
- **Mid index vs value**: `mid` is the boundary index `lo + (hi - lo) / 2`, not the array value `a[mid]`.
- **Merge loop bounds**: pointer conditions must guard against running past subarray ends (`i <= mid` and `j <= hi`).
- **Remaining elements**: remaining elements in either half must be fully copied to target array.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-heap-sort:visible:parent=sec-comparison-sort:title=Heap%20Sort -->

Relies on a heap priority structure to repeatedly place the extreme element into its final sorted position.

- Operates as a comparison sort with $\Theta(n \log n)$ running time.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-heap-foundations:visible:parent=sec-heap-sort:title=Heap%20Foundations -->

Essential heap structures and mechanics required to execute Heap Sort.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-heap-property:visible:parent=sec-heap-foundations:title=Heap%20Property -->

A complete ordered binary tree storing keys with a strict parent-child invariant.

- **Min-Heap**: $\text{parent} \le \text{children}$ (root is the minimum).
- **Max-Heap**: $\text{parent} \ge \text{children}$ (root is the maximum).
- **No sibling order**: Heap property enforces parent-child order only; sibling or adjacent array elements have no relative ordering constraint.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-heap-array-indexing:visible:parent=sec-heap-foundations:title=Array%20Representation%20%26%20Indexing -->

Stored in a 0-based sequential array without explicit node pointers.

- $\text{parent}(i) = \lfloor (i - 1) / 2 \rfloor$
- $\text{leftChild}(i) = 2i + 1$
- $\text{rightChild}(i) = 2i + 2$

**Properties**
- Node exists if and only if $\text{index} < n$ (heap size).
- Tree height grows logarithmically: $h = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$.
- Root-to-leaf path length is $O(\log n)$.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-heap-upheap-downheap:visible:parent=sec-heap-foundations:title=Upheap%20%26%20Downheap -->

Restoration procedures for disturbed heap property.

- **Upheap**:
  - Insert new key at the next free slot ($i = n$).
  - Compare with parent; swap upward until heap invariant holds or root is reached.
  - Used primarily for `add` ($O(\log n)$ path).
- **Downheap**:
  - Root disturbed or replaced by last element.
  - Compare with children; swap with the appropriate child (smaller child for min-heap, larger child for max-heap).
  - Used for `removeRoot` and Heap Sort extraction ($O(\log n)$ path).

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-heap-java-impl:visible:parent=sec-heap-foundations:title=Java%20Implementation -->

```java
// Upheap: restore invariant after adding at count
private void upheap(int i) {
    while (i > 0 && keys[(i - 1) / 2] > keys[i]) {
        swap((i - 1) / 2, i);
        i = (i - 1) / 2;
    }
}

// Downheap: restore invariant after removing root
private void downheap(int i, int n) {
    while (2 * i + 1 < n) {
        int left = 2 * i + 1;
        int right = 2 * i + 2;
        int child = left;
        if (right < n && keys[right] < keys[left]) {
            child = right;
        }
        if (keys[i] <= keys[child]) break;
        swap(i, child);
        i = child;
    }
}
```

- When swapping upward, update index $i$ to parent: `i = (i - 1) / 2`.
- Child candidates must be verified with `child < n` before array access.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-heap-sort-process:visible:parent=sec-heap-sort:title=Heap%20Sort%20Process -->

Repeatedly extract the root and place it into the shrinking boundary.

![Heap Sort: Build heap and repeatedly extract extreme element (流程与复杂度)](study/assets/asset-heap-sort-%E5%A0%86%E6%8E%92%E5%BA%8F%E6%B5%81%E7%A8%8B%E4%B8%8E%E5%A4%8D%E6%9D%82%E5%BA%A6%E4%BF%A1%E6%81%AF%E5%9B%BE.png)

**Order Rule**
- **Ascending sort**: use **Max-Heap** (max root moves to end $n-1, n-2, \dots$).
- **Descending sort**: use **Min-Heap** (min root moves to end).

**Phase Analysis**
1. **Build Heap**: bottom-up downheap takes $O(n)$ time.
2. **Sort Down**:
   - Swap root with last active element.
   - Shrink active heap range by 1.
   - Downheap new root ($O(\log n)$).
   - Repeat $n - 1$ times $\to \Theta(n \log n)$.
- Overall time complexity: $\Theta(n \log n)$ in best, worst, and average cases.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-quick-sort:visible:parent=sec-comparison-sort:title=Quick%20Sort -->

Partition around a pivot, place the pivot in its final sorted position, then recursively sort both sides.

![Quick Sort: Partition around pivot and recursively sort both sides](study/assets/asset-quick-sort-%E5%BF%AB%E9%80%9F%E6%8E%92%E5%BA%8F%E7%AE%97%E6%B3%95%E4%BF%A1%E6%81%AF%E5%9B%BE.png)

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-qs-pivot-selection:visible:parent=sec-quick-sort:title=Pivot%20Selection -->

- **First**: $lo$
- **Last**: $hi$
- **Halfway**: $lo + (hi - lo) / 2$

**Median-of-three**
- Inspect values at $a[lo]$, $a[mid]$, and $a[hi]$, where $mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2$.
- Select the value that is neither the strict minimum nor the strict maximum of the three.
- With duplicates, implementation allows a non-unique median index.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-qs-partition:visible:parent=sec-quick-sort:title=Partition -->

Rearranges subarray $a[lo \dots hi]$ around a pivot.

- **Outcome**: places pivot into its **final sorted index** $p$.
- **Return value**: returns index $p$, not the pivot value.
- **Subarray invariant**:
  - Left side ($a[lo \dots p-1]$): all values $\le$ pivot.
  - Right side ($a[p+1 \dots hi]$): all values $\ge$ pivot.
- Partition performs a single reorganization pass; it does not sort the subarrays.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-qs-pointer-rules:visible:parent=sec-qs-partition:title=Pointer%20Rules -->

When `pivot = a[hi]`:
- Pointers initialize to `left = lo`, `right = hi - 1` ($a[hi]$ reserved for pivot).
- `left` scans right to find an element $\ge \text{pivot}$ (misplaced on left).
- `right` scans left to find an element $\le \text{pivot}$ (misplaced on right).
- If `left <= right`: swap `a[left]` and `a[right]`, then `left++`, `right--`.
- When pointers cross (`left > right`): swap `a[left]` with `a[hi]`. Pivot is now at final position `left`. Return `left`.

When `pivot = a[lo]`:
- Pointers initialize to `left = lo + 1`, `right = hi`.
- After crossing: swap `a[lo]` with `a[right]`. Return `right`.

**Key Traps**
- A single partition can perform multiple internal swaps, followed by one final pivot placement swap.
- `x.compareTo(y)`:
  - `< 0` $\implies x < y$
  - `== 0` $\implies x == y$
  - `> 0` $\implies x > y$

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-qs-code:visible:parent=sec-quick-sort:title=Code -->

```java
public static void sort(Key[] a) {
    if (a.length < 2) {
        return;
    }
    sort(a, 0, a.length - 1);
}

private static void sort(Key[] a, int lo, int hi) {
    if (lo >= hi) {
        return;
    }

    int p = partition(a, lo, hi);

    sort(a, lo, p - 1);
    sort(a, p + 1, hi);
}

private static int partition(Key[] a, int lo, int hi) {
    Key pivot = a[hi];

    int left = lo;
    int right = hi - 1;

    while (left <= right) {

        while (left <= right &&
               a[left].compareTo(pivot) < 0) {
            left++;
        }

        while (left <= right &&
               a[right].compareTo(pivot) > 0) {
            right--;
        }

        if (left <= right) {
            Key.swap(a, left, right);
            left++;
            right--;
        }
    }

    Key.swap(a, left, hi);

    return left;
}
```

**Control Flow & Guard Clauses**
- `sort(a)`: whole-array entry point.
- `sort(a, lo, hi)`: Guard clause (`lo >= hi`) stops recursion; main body partitions, retrieves pivot index $p$, and recurses left and right.
- `partition`: chooses pivot, scans pointers, swaps misplaced pairs, places pivot after crossing, returns $p$.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-non-comparison-sort:visible:title=Non-comparison%20Sort -->

Sorts elements without relying solely on pairwise comparisons.

- Uses structural properties: key values, digit positions, or range intervals.
- Can surpass the $\Omega(n \log n)$ comparison lower bound under domain assumptions.
- Covered: Counting Sort, Radix Sort, Bucket Sort.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-counting-sort:visible:parent=sec-non-comparison-sort:title=Counting%20Sort -->

Count occurrences of each key directly by index, then rebuild output in order.

![Counting Sort: Direct indexing and frequency counts to rebuild in order](study/assets/asset-counting-sort-%E8%AE%A1%E6%95%B0%E6%8E%92%E5%BA%8F%EF%BC%9A%E7%BB%9F%E8%AE%A1%E5%88%B0%E6%9C%89%E5%BA%8F%E8%BE%93%E5%87%BA.png)

**Counting Sort $\neq$ Hash Table**
- **Counting Sort**: direct indexing `key -> count[key]`. The array index itself represents the value. No hash function, no collision resolution.
- **Hash Table**: `key -> h(key) -> table[index]`. Uses a hash function and handles collisions.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-counting-range-complexity:visible:parent=sec-counting-sort:title=Range%20%26%20Complexity -->

- **Dense integer range**: highly efficient when range $k$ is small relative to $n$.
- **Sparse / extreme range**: e.g., $\{1, 1000000, 1\}$ wastes memory and requires scanning empty slots.
- **Offset handling**: if values range over $[\min \dots \max]$, allocate size $\max - \min + 1$ with index `val - min`.
- **Complexity**: $\Theta(n + k)$
  - $k$ = key range size
  - only if $k = O(n) \to \Theta(n)$
  - if $k \gg n$, $k$ dominates
  - Example: $n = 100, k = 1{,}000{,}000 \to \text{not } \Theta(n)$

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-counting-code:visible:parent=sec-counting-sort:title=Code -->

```java
static void countingSort(int[] numbers, int k) {

    // 1. 开 count
    int[] count = new int[k];

    // 2. 数每个数字出现几次
    for (int number : numbers) {
        count[number]++;
    }

    // 3. 把次数变成右边界
    for (int i = 1; i < count.length; i++) {
        count[i] += count[i - 1];
    }

    // 4. 开 output
    int[] output = new int[numbers.length];

    // 5. 从右往左，把每个数放到自己的位置
    for (int i = numbers.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        int number = numbers[i];

        count[number]--;

        output[count[number]] = number;
    }

    // 6. copy back
    for (int i = 0; i < numbers.length; i++) {
        numbers[i] = output[i];
    }
}
```

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-counting-stable-object:visible:parent=sec-counting-sort:title=Stable%20%2B%20object -->

same key ≠ same record
record = key + payload / ID

count key → move whole record
4A, 2X, 4B → 2X, 4A, 4B

stable → equal keys keep relative order
right-boundary version → scan input right → left

⚠ wrapper/object 保留 identity
⚠ stable 由 placement order 保证，不是 wrapper 本身保证

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-radix-sort:visible:parent=sec-non-comparison-sort:title=Radix%20Sort -->

Sort multi-digit keys digit by digit, from least significant digit (LSD) to most significant digit (MSD).

![Radix Sort: LSD to MSD digit passes with stable sub-sorts](study/assets/asset-radix-sort-%E5%9F%BA%E6%95%B0%E6%8E%92%E5%BA%8F%EF%BC%9A%E9%80%90%E4%BD%8D%E7%A8%B3%E5%AE%9A%E6%8E%92%E5%BA%8F%E6%B5%81%E7%A8%8B.png)

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-radix-stability:visible:parent=sec-radix-sort:title=Stability -->

- **Definition**: elements with equal keys preserve their prior relative order.
- **Why Radix requires stability**: earlier passes establish correct lower-digit order. A later pass must not disrupt this relative order when current digits match.
- **Reusing buckets**: each decimal pass partitions into digits $0 \dots 9$, reusing the same 10 counters / buckets.
- **Complexity**: $\Theta(d(n + k))$ where $d = \text{digits}$, $k = \text{radix}$ (10 for decimal). For fixed $d$, time is $\Theta(n)$.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-radix-code:visible:parent=sec-radix-sort:title=Code -->

```java
static void radixSort(int[] numbers) {

    if (numbers.length <= 1) {
        return;
    }

    // Find max
    int max = numbers[0];

    for (int number : numbers) {
        if (number > max) {
            max = number;
        }
    }

    // Ones → tens → hundreds → ...
    for (int exp = 1; max / exp > 0; exp *= 10) {
        countingSortByDigit(numbers, exp);
    }
}


static void countingSortByDigit(int[] numbers, int exp) {

    int[] count = new int[10];

    // Count current digit
    for (int number : numbers) {
        int digit = (number / exp) % 10;
        count[digit]++;
    }

    // Cumulative boundaries
    for (int i = 1; i < count.length; i++) {
        count[i] += count[i - 1];
    }

    int[] output = new int[numbers.length];

    // Stable placement: right → left
    for (int i = numbers.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {

        int number = numbers[i];
        int digit = (number / exp) % 10;

        count[digit]--;
        output[count[digit]] = number;
    }

    // Copy back
    for (int i = 0; i < numbers.length; i++) {
        numbers[i] = output[i];
    }
}
```

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-bucket-sort:visible:parent=sec-non-comparison-sort:title=Bucket%20Sort -->

Distribute elements across equal-width value intervals (buckets), sort within each bucket, and concatenate.

![Bucket Sort: Distribute into equal-width buckets, sort, and concatenate](study/assets/asset-bucket-sort-%E6%A1%B6%E6%8E%92%E5%BA%8F%E6%B5%81%E7%A8%8B%E4%BF%A1%E6%81%AF%E5%9B%BE.png)

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-bucket-distribution:visible:parent=sec-bucket-sort:title=Distribution -->

- Value domain is partitioned into equal-width buckets (e.g., $B_0: [0, 9], B_1: [10, 19], B_2: [20, 29]$).
- **Equal-width $\neq$ equal count**: equal interval size does not guarantee equal element counts.
- Boundaries are designed from the known input range, not chosen randomly.
- **Uniform distribution requirement**: near-linear performance relies on roughly uniform input distribution.
- **Floating-point index formula**: for values in $[0, 1)$ with 10 buckets: $\text{index} = \lfloor 10 \times \text{value} \rfloor$ (e.g., $0.46 \implies \lfloor 4.6 \rfloor = \text{bucket } 4$).

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-bucket-worst-case:visible:parent=sec-bucket-sort:title=Worst%20Case -->

- Standard implementation sorts inside buckets using **Insertion Sort**.
- **Expected / Average time**: $\Theta(n)$ when elements distribute uniformly.
- **Worst-case time**: $\Theta(n^2)$ when all $n$ elements collapse into a single bucket and degrade to Insertion Sort on $n$ items.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-selection:visible:title=Selection -->

Finds a specific order statistic or rank without sorting the entire collection.

- Distinct category from sorting algorithms.
- Primary method: Quickselect.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-quickselect:visible:parent=sec-selection:title=Quickselect -->

Partition array around a pivot like Quick Sort, but recurse only into the side containing the target rank.

![Quickselect: Partition around pivot and prune unneeded side to find k-th order statistic](study/assets/asset-quickselect-Quickselect%20%E7%AE%97%E6%B3%95%E6%B5%81%E7%A8%8B%E4%BF%A1%E6%81%AF%E5%9B%BE.png)

- Selection algorithm, not a sorting algorithm.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-quickselect-order-statistics:visible:parent=sec-quickselect:title=Order%20Statistics -->

The $i$-th order statistic is the $i$-th smallest element in sorted order.

- Minimum = 1st smallest.
- Maximum = $n$-th smallest.
- Median = middle rank ($\lfloor (n + 1) / 2 \rfloor$).

**Single Minimum or Maximum (单独找)**
- $n - 1$ comparisons (track current min/max, compare against each remaining element).
- $\Theta(n)$ time.

**Simultaneous Minimum + Maximum (同时找 · Pairing)**
- naive $\to 2n - 2$ comparisons
- better: process pairs
  - $a$ vs $b$
  - smaller $\to$ compare with min
  - larger $\to$ compare with max
- **odd $n$**:
  - first element $\to$ both min and max
  - rest $\to$ process in pairs
  - comparisons: $3\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$
- **even $n$**:
  - compare first two once: smaller $\to$ min, larger $\to$ max
  - rest $\to$ process in pairs
  - comparisons: $3n/2 - 2$
- $\approx 3n/2$ comparisons, still $\Theta(n)$
- Recognize the process: pair first $\to$ smaller to min, larger to max

**Quiz Trap**
- $i$-th smallest $\ne$ value $i$.
- Example: in $\{1, 11, 12, 6, 13, 18\}$, sorted is $\{1, 6, 11, 12, 13, 18\}$. The 6th smallest element is 18, not 6.

<!-- nodal-panel:sec-quickselect-relation-qs:visible:parent=sec-quickselect:title=Relation%20to%20Quick%20Sort -->

- **Quick Sort**: partitions, then recurses into **both** sides until fully sorted.
- **Quickselect**: partitions using the same routine as [Quick Sort / Partition](nodal://node/cis223-sorting-selection/sec-qs-partition), then recurses **only** into the subarray containing the target rank.

**Pivot Rank Discovery**
- Choosing a pivot does not reveal its rank beforehand.
- Partitioning places the pivot into its final index $p$ and establishes that $p$ elements precede it.
- If $p == \text{target index}$: done; pivot is the answer.
- If $\text{target index} < p$: recurse only on left.
- If $\text{target index} > p$: recurse only on right.
- Average time $\Theta(n)$; worst case $\Theta(n^2)$.
